advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST-structure assertions in test_security_pin_main_uses_aware_now_local_date_not_date_today with a behavioral test that monkeypatches the clock/local tz and asserts main() derives the correct local calendar date (observable freshness date), not the source's syntax.
evidence: assert not today_calls, "main() must not call date.today() (DTZ011)"
assert now_calls, "main() must obtain an aware current instant via datetime.now(tz=...)"
Litmus (Rule 4): renaming/extracting the date derivation in main() into a helper preserves behavior yet fails these AST assertions.
advisory.finding: test_security_pin_main_uses_aware_now_local_date_not_date_today asserts on the AST of the source under test (security_pin.py) — it reads security_pin.__file__, ast.parses it, and asserts main() contains no .today() call and does contain a now(tz=...) + .date() chain. This is source-grepping / a change-detector: it verifies the implementation's TEXT/structure, not observable behavior, and would break on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. extracting the current-date derivation into a module-level _today() helper, or spelling the aware-now differently) with no behavior change. There is no behavioral test of main()'s date source (e.g. monkeypatching the clock and asserting the freshness date used).
